If the **SEARCH** expression doesn't include required metric dimensions, then CloudWatch can't match the query to existing metrics.\\n\\nTo resolve this issue, use the CloudWatch console or AWS CLI to identify the required dimensions. Then, add the required dimensions to your **SEARCH** expression.\\n\\n**Use the CloudWatch console**\\n\\nComplete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Open the [CloudWatch console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/).\\n2. Choose **Metrics**, and then select your namespace.\\n3. Choose **Graphed metrics**, and then choose **Details**.\\n\\n**Use the AWS CLI**\\n\\nRun the following **list-metrics** command:\\n\\n```plaintext\\naws cloudwatch list-metrics --namespace NAMESPACE --region REGION\\n```\\n\\n**Note:** Replace **NAMESPACE** with your namespace and **REGION** with your AWS Region.\\n\\nThe output shows the metric name and all dimensions for each metric, such as **WorkGroup** and **QueryType**. Also, note the dimension's values.\\n\\n**Include dimensions in your SEARCH expression**\\n\\n**Note:** In the following commands, replace **NAMESPACE** with your namespace. Replace **DIMENSION-NAMES** with the comma-separated dimension names, for example **WorkGroup,QueryType**. Replace **METRIC-NAME** with the name of your metric and **REGION** with your Region. Replace **STATISTIC** with the statistic to retrieve, such as **Sum** or **Average**.\\n\\nRun the following **get-metric-data** command to include the dimensions in your **SEARCH** expression:\\n\\n```plaintext\\naws cloudwatch get-metric-data --metric-data-queries '[{\\\"Id\\\":\\\"m1\\\",\\\"Expression\\\":\\\"SEARCH('{NAMESPACE,DIMENSION-NAMES} YOUR-METRIC-NAME','Average',86400)\\\",\\\"Period\\\":86400}]' --start-time START-TIME --end-time END-TIME --region REGION\\n```\\n\\nIf the **SEARCH** expression continues to return empty results, then run the following **get-metric-data** command to query the specific metric with all dimensions:\\n\\n```plaintext\\naws cloudwatch get-metric-data \\\\\\n --metric-data-queries '[{\\\"Id\\\": \\\"m1\\\", \\\"MetricStat\\\": {\\\"Metric\\\": {\\\"Namespace\\\": \\\"NAMESPACE\\\", \\\"MetricName\\\": \\\"METRIC-NAME\\\", \\\"Dimensions\\\": [{\\\"Name\\\":\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/cloudwatch-metric-gaps-discrepancies\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"GetMetricDataResponse Class | AWS SDK for .NET Version 4\",\"context\":\"## Class\\n\\nSearch:\\n\\nEntire Site\\nArticles & Tutorials\\nDocumentation\\nDocumentation - {"id": "ef528a21-4424-4f1f-8d37-d5b117c821db", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "That confirms `GetMetricData` (or `GetMetricStatistics`) is the standard CloudWatch retrieval mechanism, using `Sum` as the statistic for these usage-time metrics, dimensioned by `AgentSpaceUUID` and queried per namespace/metric name. Here's the report:

## AWS DevOps Agent Daily Cost — space-123

**Note:** PromQL query returned no data for this AgentSpace, so this report uses the supplied CloudWatch daily sums directly, per your instruction not to call AWS.

| Metric | Seconds | Rate ($/sec) | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| ConsumedInvestigationTime | 100 | $0.0083 | $0.83 |
| ConsumedEvaluationTime | 20 | $0.0083 | $0.166 |
| ConsumedOnDemandTime | 30 | $0.0083 | $0.249 |
| ConsumedReleaseReadinessReviewTime | 50 | $0.0083 | $0.415 |
| **Total** | **200** | — | **$1.66** |

**Gross direct cost = 200 seconds × $0.0083/sec = $1.66/day** for AgentSpace `space-123`.

(This is *gross* — it doesn't net out any AWS Support monthly credits, which are applied separately against AWS DevOps Agent charges.)

### How these values are normally retrieved

These four metrics (`ConsumedInvestigationTime`, `ConsumedEvaluationTime`, `ConsumedOnDemandTime`, `ConsumedReleaseReadinessReviewTime`) are CloudWatch usage metrics emitted with an `AgentSpaceUUID` dimension. The standard way to pull them is the CloudWatch **`GetMetricData`** API (or its older sibling `GetMetricStatistics`), requesting the **`Sum`** statistic over a daily (86400-second) period, scoped to the relevant namespace and filtered by the `AgentSpaceUUID` dimension value (`space-123` in this case). `GetMetricData` is preferred over `GetMetricStatistics` for multi-metric batch retrieval since it supports querying several metrics/expressions in a single call, which is typical when building a cost rollup across all four consumption metrics at once.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
